Jessica the jackrabbit wants to climb down a wall. The wall consists of 2026 horizontal layers stacked vertically. The $n$th layer from the top is partitioned into $2^n - 1$ identical rectangular bricks arranged side by side. Jessica begins in the topmost layer, which contains a single brick. A move consists of Jessica going down one layer to a brick that shares a side with the brick she is currently on.

Determine, with proof, the total number of distinct sequences of moves Jessica can take to reach the 2026th layer.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We interpret “shares a side” as sharing a positive-length segment of a horizontal side between adjacent layers.

All horizontal layers of the wall have the same total width. Scale this width to \(1\).

For a fixed layer \(n\), let

\[
k=2^n-1.
\]

Then layer \(n\) has \(k\) bricks, and layer \(n+1\) has

\[
2^{n+1}-1=2k+1
\]

bricks.

Number the bricks in each layer from left to right. The \(i\)-th brick in layer \(n\) spans the horizontal interval

\[
\left[\frac{i-1}{k},\frac{i}{k}\right].
\]

The \(j\)-th brick in layer \(n+1\) spans

\[
\left[\frac{j-1}{2k+1},\frac{j}{2k+1}\right].
\]

These two bricks share a side exactly when their horizontal intervals overlap in more than a point, i.e.

\[
\frac{i-1}{k}<\frac{j}{2k+1}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{j-1}{2k+1}<\frac{i}{k}.
\]

The first inequality gives

\[
j> \frac{(i-1)(2k+1)}{k}
=2i-2+\frac{i-1}{k}.
\]

The second gives

\[
j< \frac{i(2k+1)}{k}+1
=2i+1+\frac{i}{k}.
\]

Since \(1\le i\le k\),

\[
2i-2\le 2i-2+\frac{i-1}{k}<2i-1
\]

and

\[
2i+1<2i+1+\frac{i}{k}\le 2i+2.
\]

Therefore the only integers \(j\) satisfying both inequalities are

\[
j=2i-1,\quad 2i,\quad 2i+1.
\]

Thus every brick in layer \(n\) shares a side with exactly three bricks in layer \(n+1\).

Jessica must make \(2026-1=2025\) moves to reach the \(2026\)th layer. At each move, there are exactly \(3\) possible bricks to move to, regardless of which brick she is currently on. Hence the number of distinct sequences of moves is

\[
3^{2025}.
\]

\[
\boxed{3^{2025}}
\]
